claims.text: The identity of X (Al, Mn, or Si) governs protective-oxide formation and persistence in CrFeCoNiX alloys above 900 °C.
Al preferentially forms a protective Al2O3-based scale because of favorable oxidation thermodynamics.
Al2O3 scales grow slowly relative to chromium oxide scales.
Low oxygen diffusivity through the Al2O3 scale ensures its coherence and adhesion.
The Al-containing alloy develops a continuous, coherent, adherent, fine-grained Al2O3-based scale.
The Al2O3-based scale persists at 950 °C with minimal spallation.
Mn oxides in the Mn-containing alloy are less thermodynamically stable than the protective oxide formed in the Al-containing alloy.
Si oxides in the Si-containing alloy are less thermodynamically stable than the protective oxide formed in the Al-containing alloy.
The Mn-containing alloy develops a discontinuous, porous oxide scale prone to cracking and spallation.
The Si-containing alloy develops a discontinuous, porous oxide scale prone to cracking and spallation.
Mn- and Si-derived oxides have higher volatility, lower adhesion energies, or lower cohesiveness than the Al-derived scale.
Discontinuous and porous Mn- or Si-containing scales cause accelerated oxidation and degradation.
Al2O3 provides resistance to high-temperature oxidation and corrosion, including environments containing aggressive carbon or sulfur species.
Alloy chemistry and microstructure influence the composition and variability of oxide scales in high-entropy alloys.
Approximately 100 hours at 950 °C is sufficient to produce a mature oxide layer for the proposed comparison.
The comparison will hold X identity as the intended compositional variable while controlling processing, phase state, grain size, defect density, and segregation.
Failure of the Al-containing alloy to produce a significantly more continuous, coherent, and adherent scale than both comparator alloys would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis characterizes Si-derived oxides as less thermodynamically stable and less protective, whereas cited record PMC6356250::web::054::5_3_oxidation explicitly states that SiO2, like Al2O3, is highly stable and desirable for oxidation protection above 1000 °C.
